name: pdf-inspector
description: Fast Rust library for PDF inspection, classification, and text extraction. Intelligently detects scanned vs text-based PDFs to enable smart routing decisions.
one_liner: A fast tool that looks at a PDF and instantly tells you whether it's a real digital document or just a scanned image — so you know whether to extract the text directly or run it through OCR first.
buyer: A document-processing SaaS or back-office operations team (invoices, mortgages, legal filings) that needs to route thousands of incoming PDFs to the right processing pipeline without wasting compute on unnecessary OCR.
business_use_cases: An invoice-automation company uses it to instantly route scanned invoices to OCR and digital invoices to direct text extraction, cutting processing cost.
A mortgage or legal-tech company classifies incoming document batches before running expensive AI extraction only where needed.
A due-diligence data room tool pre-screens uploaded PDFs to flag which ones need manual review because OCR quality will be poor.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a hosted 'smart document router' API that plugs into existing document pipelines and bills per document classified.

steal_this: Wrap it in a simple API this weekend that takes a PDF and returns 'scanned' or 'text' plus a routing recommendation, and pitch it to a document-heavy back-office team as a cost-saving preprocessing step.
